description: Handles (PROTOCOL 21, ADR 0015 revision 2): the grammar (what a person types -> a canonical nick.digits, or why not, including Unicode look-alikes and every reserved nick); labels (Argon2id of the canonical handle, production parameters, plus small-parameter answers for checking an independent Argon2id); owner, introduction and recovery keys from seeds, the introduction seed giving both intro (Ed25519) and xintro (X25519, by HKDF); claim, update and recover records with their publish inputs and signatures; owner-rule histories with their verdicts, among them versions that are not the label's next and signatures only a lenient verifier takes (sig_made); values that are not records, among them keys of small order and keys at or above p; a contact request sealed to xintro and opened with the introduction identity; proof-of-work stamps at low difficulty over that envelope, with the cases a relay refuses; and an introduction acknowledgement with the cases a requester refuses. The log (21.5) and the relay (21.6) pin their own halves elsewhere.

grammar.nick: 3-20 of [a-z0-9_], first a letter, no "__", not ending "_"
grammar.digits: 2-6 ASCII digits, compared as a string
grammar.normalisation: trim ASCII whitespace (U+0009-U+000D, U+0020), remove ONE leading "@", lower-case A-Z; nothing else is folded

valid.note: one leading @ removed and A-Z lower-cased
digits are a string: 042 is a different handle from 42
an underscore inside the nick, and a leading zero kept
six digits, and a digit inside the nick
the shortest nick and the fewest digits
a reserved nick with a letter added is not reserved

invalid.note: trimming happens before the @ is removed, not after
a no-break space (U+00A0) is not trimmed: only ASCII whitespace is
Cyrillic і (U+0456) in place of Latin i
Cyrillic а (U+0430) in place of Latin a: a reserved nick's look-alike
the Kelvin sign (U+212A), which Unicode lower-cases to ASCII k
long s (U+017F), which Unicode upper-cases to ASCII S
dotted capital I (U+0130), which Unicode lower-cases to i + a combining dot

record_rules.version: each entry is the label's next: a claim is 1, every later entry the current + 1
